title: Tyra Banks Wears Emerald Lehenga for Maneesh Goyal's New York Diwali Party
excerpt: In her first complete traditional Indian look, Banks wore a custom Maison Tai lehenga and a Kalyan Jewellers diamond set from its New Jersey showroom — and praised the paneer.
body:
• Supermodel Tyra Banks wore a complete traditional Indian look for the first time — an emerald-green and gold lehenga custom-made by Maison Tai — for a Diwali celebration at her friend Maneesh Goyal's home in New York.
  • Her jewellery was a handcrafted open-setting natural diamond set from Kalyan Jewellers' New Jersey showroom: a choker, jhumka earrings, a maang tikka, an odiyanam waist belt and a ring.
  • Banks documented the evening on Instagram, praising the meaning of Diwali as Goyal shared it with guests, the Passerine NYC catering — and her paneer — and her seat next to Ricki Lake.

Tyra Banks has done her first full Desi look, and she did not do it halfway. The supermodel and television host stepped out for a Diwali celebration in New York in an emerald-green and gold lehenga with a complete set of traditional diamond jewellery — and documented the evening for her Instagram followers as, in her words, a celebration of light, love and culture.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DfgDC0EnQn7/

The celebration was hosted by her friend Maneesh Goyal at his home. Banks' lehenga — a structured blouse with an intricately embellished skirt — was custom-designed for the occasion by the fashion house Maison Tai, according to Indulge Express. The jewellery, sourced from Kalyan Jewellers' showroom in New Jersey, was a handcrafted suite in traditional open-setting natural diamonds: a choker necklace, hanging jhumka earrings, a maang tikka, an odiyanam waist belt and a statement ring. The jeweller noted it was its second Diwali celebration in the United States since opening the Edison, New Jersey showroom.

"Green and gold, baby! Got all dolled up for my friend Maneesh Goyal's Diwali celebration, and honeyyyy… between my green and gold and the bold spices on the menu, the assignment was UNDERSTOOD!"

— Tyra Banks, on Instagram

Inside the evening

Banks' caption described a host who treated the festival as something to be shared, not just staged: Goyal welcomed guests into his home and shared the story and meaning of Diwali. He also, she wrote, played "friendship matchmaker" and seated her next to Ricki Lake. The food was catered by Passerine NYC, and Banks singled out the paneer: she was, she wrote, still thinking about the sauce it was served in.

Why it registers

Diwali in New York has moved well beyond the diaspora's own calendar — city halls, schools and now private salons in Manhattan host it, and the guest lists mix accordingly. A first full traditional look from a figure of Banks' stature, styled with a named Indian jeweller's New Jersey showroom rather than a costume approximation, is the fashion version of that shift: the festival as an occasion American hosts mark properly, with Indian houses supplying the craft.

Banks began modelling at 15 and broke barriers as the first African American woman to appear on the covers of major fashion and sports magazines. Her Diwali post gave the festival — and the Indian designers and jewellers behind the look — an audience of millions who may never have seen a maang tikka named before.
